verdict.rationale: Unleash's docs say each environment has its own feature flag configuration, so a flag can be enabled in development or test without being enabled in production. Backend API tokens are scoped to one or more projects and a single environment, which delivers environment-scoped SDK keys. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the environment and token scoping workflow (the evidence is first-party docs only).

support.subject: As a developer, I can manage separate environments (dev/staging/prod) with independent flag states and scoped SDK keys

citations.quote: each environment has different feature flag configurations. This allows you to enable a flag in development or test without enabling it in production.
Environments represent different stages in your development lifecycle. They allow you to manage your product releases from local development to production.
Backend tokens are scoped to one or more projects and a single environment.
When creating a backend token, you can give it access to a specific list of projects or to all current or future projects.
